Question: Q01. DMA transfer on STM32F4 corrupts data when source and destination are in same SRAM bank
Answer: Check AHB bus matrix arbitration and ensure DMA streams accessing the same SRAM bank do not cause contention. Use different SRAM banks for source and destination buffers, or serialize accesses with proper DMA stream priority.

Question: Q02. USB OTG HS in FS mode drops packets under heavy CDC traffic on STM32F4
Answer: Verify FIFO depth allocation for each endpoint, ensure RX FIFO is large enough for back-to-back packets, and check that NAK handling in the driver does not discard valid frames. Increase FIFO sizes and validate with USB analyzer.

Question: Q03. FreeRTOS tick drift when using TIM as timebase instead of SysTick on F4
Answer: Ensure timer prescaler and period produce exact 1ms overflow, verify NVIC priority does not block tick ISR, and confirm no other ISR with same or higher priority runs long enough to delay tick processing.

Question: Q04. Ethernet on STM32F407 works initially but stops receiving after several hours
Answer: Check DMA descriptor ring management, ensure RX descriptors are properly returned to DMA ownership, verify cache coherency if MPU is configured, and monitor ETH_DMASR for buffer unavailable condition.

Question: Q05. ADC multimode dual simultaneous on F4 gives inconsistent readings between ADC1 and ADC2
Answer: Verify both ADCs share exact same sampling time and trigger source, check that common data register is read atomically, and ensure no channel conflict. External trigger synchronization must be deterministic.

Question: Q06. SDIO 4-bit wide bus mode fails on custom board but works on Nucleo
Answer: Check signal integrity on DAT0-DAT3 lines, verify pull-ups, ensure SDIO clock does not exceed card capability without proper initialization sequence, and validate that card properly acknowledged bus width switch command.

Question: Q07. SPI DMA circular mode produces gap between frames on STM32F4
Answer: The gap comes from DMA half-transfer and transfer-complete ISR overhead. Use double-buffering with DMA stream FIFO threshold, minimize ISR processing, and verify that SPI CR1 is not temporarily disabled between frames.

Question: Q08. IWDG resets system during Flash erase on STM32F4
Answer: Flash erase blocks CPU for several milliseconds on F4. Feed IWDG before starting erase, or use page-by-page erase with watchdog refresh between pages. Alternatively increase IWDG prescaler to allow for worst-case erase time.

Question: Q09. CAN bus-off recovery does not complete automatically on STM32F4
Answer: Check CAN initialization mode flags, verify ABOM bit is set for automatic bus-off management, and ensure physical layer allows bus idle detection. Without ABOM, software must manually initiate recovery sequence.

Question: Q10. STM32F4 Discovery board MEMS accelerometer readings have excessive noise
Answer: Verify SPI clock polarity and phase match LIS3DSH requirements, check PCB grounding near sensor, apply digital low-pass filtering, and ensure sampling rate is appropriate for application bandwidth needs.

Question: Q11. RTC alarm interrupt fires twice on STM32F4
Answer: Clear alarm flag and EXTI pending bit in correct order inside ISR. If EXTI line 17 pending is not cleared before RTC alarm flag, the interrupt can retrigger immediately after exit.

Question: Q12. DMA memory-to-memory transfer on F4 is slower than expected
Answer: F4 DMA controllers have limited memory-to-memory bandwidth due to AHB bus sharing. Use FIFO burst mode, align buffers to 32-bit boundaries, and select optimal burst size. For large copies, consider using memcpy with core for better throughput.

Question: Q13. STM32F4 enters HardFault when accessing backup registers without enabling PWR clock
Answer: Backup domain access requires PWR peripheral clock enabled and DBP bit set in PWR_CR. Without this sequence, any access to RTC or backup SRAM generates a bus fault. Enable RCC_APB1ENR_PWREN first.

Question: Q14. FDCAN message lost on STM32H5 when using hardware filters in range mode
Answer: Verify filter element configuration in SRAM, ensure message RAM allocation does not overlap between filters and FIFOs, and check that range boundaries include expected IDs. Validate with single acceptance filter first.

Question: Q15. TrustZone configuration on H5 causes bus fault when accessing GPIO from non-secure world
Answer: Map the GPIO peripheral as non-secure in GTZC MPCBB or TZSC registers, configure SAU for correct memory partitioning, and verify that GPIOA_SECCFGR bits allow non-secure pin access. Order matters in security attribute configuration.

Question: Q16. HASH peripheral on STM32H5 gives wrong digest when input is not 32-bit aligned
Answer: Use MDMAT bit for multi-buffer hashing, pad final block correctly, and handle byte-level input with HASH_DIN register byte access mode. Misaligned DMA transfers will also produce incorrect results.

Question: Q17. ICACHE performance benefit is not measurable on STM32H5 after enabling
Answer: Invalidate ICACHE fully after enabling, ensure code under test is in cacheable region defined by MPU, and measure with enough iterations to amortize cold-start misses. First run always shows cache fill penalty.

Question: Q18. Secure boot on H5 fails after OB key provisioning
Answer: Verify option byte programming sequence, ensure RDP level transition is intentional, check that secure boot address matches application vector table, and validate BFB2 and swap bank bits. Incorrect OB can brick the device.

Question: Q19. USB PD on STM32H5 UCPD peripheral does not negotiate 9V with charger
Answer: Check dead battery pull-down, verify CC line configuration, ensure UCPD PHY is properly initialized with correct trim values, and validate PDO advertisement in source capabilities response. Monitor CC state machine transitions.

Question: Q20. DMA linked-list mode on H5 creates circular dependency and locks up
Answer: Verify linked-list node addresses do not form unintended loops, ensure CLLR register points to valid SRAM locations, and check that terminal node has link pointer cleared. Use DMA transfer error interrupt to detect lockup.

Question: Q21. LPBAM autonomous mode on STM32H5 does not wake peripherals correctly
Answer: LPBAM requires specific peripheral clock enable sequences preserved across low-power entry. Verify autonomous mode enable bits, DMA trigger configuration for low-power, and that target peripheral supports LPBAM wakeup path.

Question: Q22. External interrupt on H5 is missed after exiting STOP mode
Answer: Ensure EXTI line is not masked during stop entry, wakeup source is properly configured in PWR registers, and pending bit is checked after wakeup. GPIO must retain configuration across low-power state.

Question: Q23. Flash ECC error occurs randomly on STM32H5 after many write cycles
Answer: Monitor ECCR flags, implement ECC error handler that logs address and corrects single-bit or reports double-bit, and avoid writing same flash location repeatedly. Consider wear-leveling for frequently updated storage.

Question: Q24. OSPI HyperRAM latency is higher than datasheet value on H5
Answer: Verify fixed latency vs variable latency configuration matches RAM device, check clock frequency against device AC timing, and ensure MPU attributes allow write-through or write-back caching on OSPI mapped region.

Question: Q25. CRC peripheral on H5 produces different result than software implementation
Answer: Check polynomial, initial value, input/output data reversal settings, and data width configuration. CRC_POL, CRC_INIT, and bit reversal in CRC_CR must exactly match software reference parameters.

Question: Q26. STM32U5 STOP2 current is 50uA instead of expected 2uA
Answer: Audit all GPIO configurations for floating inputs, disable unused peripheral clocks, verify no debug connection draws current, check SMPS vs LDO selection, and ensure SRAM retention is minimized. Use power shield for accurate measurement.

Question: Q27. LPUART wakeup from STOP2 on U5 drops first received character
Answer: Configure wakeup on start bit or address match, ensure LPUART clock source survives STOP2, and add protocol preamble byte. Clock restoration latency from LSE or HSI must be shorter than first byte duration.

Question: Q28. ADF peripheral on STM32U5 produces distorted audio from digital microphone
Answer: Verify clock frequency matches PDM microphone specification, check decimation filter configuration and gain settings, ensure DMA circular buffer is properly sized for audio frame, and validate bit clock phase.

Question: Q29. GTZC violation triggers immediately after enabling TrustZone on U5
Answer: Check that all memory and peripheral security attributes are configured before enabling SAU and GTZC. Default state after TZ enable may block previously accessible resources. Configure MPCBB for SRAM and TZSC for peripherals first.

Question: Q30. MDF filter output saturates on STM32U5 even with low input signal
Answer: Review gain chain from microphone to MDF output, check OFFSET and SHIFT values in filter configuration, verify INTEGRATOR mode settings, and ensure output format bit width accommodates full dynamic range.

Question: Q31. LPTIMER on U5 does not count during STOP2 with LSE clock
Answer: Verify LPTIM clock source is LSE in RCC_CCIPR, ensure LPTIM is started before entering STOP2, and check that LPTIM autonomous mode bit is set. Peripheral must be fully running before CPU stops.

Question: Q32. USB Type-C on STM32U5 fails PD contract when VBUS rises slowly
Answer: Adjust UCPD dead battery exit timing, verify VBUS detection thresholds, and ensure PD state machine handles slow ramp scenarios. Add debouncing on VBUS monitoring and validate attach/detach sequence.

Question: Q33. Secure key storage in STM32U5 OTP returns all zeros after provisioning
Answer: Check that OTP programming voltage and timing requirements are met, verify lock state of target OTP area, and ensure read is performed from correct secure context. Locked OTP cannot be reprogrammed.

Question: Q34. TouchSensing on STM32U5 has poor sensitivity after entering low-power mode
Answer: Recalibrate TSC charge transfer parameters after wakeup, ensure GPIO analog switch settings are restored, verify shield electrode configuration, and allow stabilization time before first acquisition.

Question: Q35. OCTOSPI memory-mapped read on U5 returns stale data after write through indirect mode
Answer: Invalidate ICACHE and DCACHE after indirect write operations, or use a cache-bypass region for frequently written data. Memory-mapped reads serve cached content that does not reflect indirect writes.

Question: Q36. PKA RSA signature verification is extremely slow on STM32U5
Answer: PKA hardware accelerator needs correct operand length configuration and RAM input formatting. Verify modulus size matches actual key length, precompute Montgomery parameter, and ensure no software fallback is triggered by parameter error.

Question: Q37. ThreadX on U5 consumes more power than bare-metal equivalent
Answer: Enable ThreadX low-power module, implement idle processing hook that enters STOP2, and ensure tick timer uses LPTIM in tickless mode. Default idle loop without power management keeps CPU in run mode.

Question: Q38. SRAM4 retention in STOP3 mode does not preserve data on STM32U5
Answer: Verify SRAM4 retention enable bits in PWR_CR1, check that SRAM4 is not powered down by supply configuration, and validate with simple write-sleep-read test before trusting complex data structures.

Question: Q39. SubGHz radio on STM32WL does not transmit despite register configuration matching datasheet
Answer: Check RF switch control GPIO configuration, verify PA and SMPS regulators are correctly selected for target power, ensure BUSY line is released before SPI commands, and validate matching network for target frequency.

Question: Q40. LoRa reception sensitivity is 10dB worse than expected on STM32WL
Answer: Check TCXO startup time, verify LNA boost configuration, ensure frequency calibration was performed, and validate antenna matching network at exact operating frequency. Board layout parasitic can degrade sensitivity.

Question: Q41. STM32WL dual-core CM4 cannot access radio peripheral
Answer: On STM32WL55, radio is accessible only from CM0+ core by default. Configure IPCC for inter-core radio command passing, or remap peripheral access through SYSCFG if single-core variant supports it.

Question: Q42. IPCC communication between CM4 and CM0+ on WL drops messages under load
Answer: Implement flow control on IPCC channels, check that RX occupied flag is cleared only after message is fully processed, and ensure priority inversion between cores does not block flag acknowledgment.

Question: Q43. Deep sleep current on STM32WL is high due to SubGHz radio not entering sleep
Answer: Send explicit Sleep command to radio before CPU stop entry, verify SPI communication completed successfully, check BUSY pin goes low confirming radio entered sleep, and disable radio regulator if unused.

Question: Q44. Frequency hopping on WL introduces packet loss at channel boundaries
Answer: Reduce settling time by pre-calibrating radio for all channels, use image rejection calibration per frequency range, ensure PLL lock is confirmed before TX/RX, and add guard time at hop transitions.

Question: Q45. STM32WL LoRaWAN OTAA join fails despite correct DevEUI and AppKey
Answer: Verify byte order of DevEUI and AppKey matches network server expectation (MSB vs LSB), check Join Request MIC calculation, ensure datarate and channel plan match gateway configuration, and validate RX1/RX2 timing windows.

Question: Q46. RTC on STM32WL drifts significantly after extended radio TX activity
Answer: High current draw during TX can cause voltage droop affecting LSE oscillator. Verify power supply decoupling, consider using LSE CSS, and apply smooth calibration. Check if TXCO is shared with RTC path.

Question: Q47. Flash write during LoRa RX window causes packet loss on STM32WL
Answer: Flash programming halts CPU and bus for duration of write. Schedule Flash operations outside RX windows, use double buffering for received data, or implement write queueing that respects radio timing constraints.

Question: Q48. STM32WL custom bootloader breaks radio calibration after jump to application
Answer: Radio calibration data stored during manufacturing must be preserved across boot transitions. Save SubGHz_Phy calibration values before jumping and restore after application startup, or avoid full radio reset in application init.

Question: Q49. Sigfox uplink on WL passes certification pre-test but fails production spectrum mask
Answer: Verify PA ramp time, modulation parameters, and exact frequency offset at temperature extremes. Production test with cold start may reveal calibration issues not seen in lab. Apply frequency trimming per device.

Question: Q50. STM32WL long-range mode reaches only half the expected outdoor range
Answer: Check antenna gain and radiation pattern, verify TX power configuration including PA and SMPS settings, ensure spreading factor and bandwidth are optimal for range, and validate link budget accounting for connector and cable losses.
